extracted.intended_audience: short-story writers, editors, anthology compilers, literary critics, and students of creative writing
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative criteria and selection judgments for American short stories (early 20th-century), focusing on qualities editors/critics use to judge and choose the year's best stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray spiritual values without sentimentality
rubrics_metrics.description: Portraying the spiritual values of a small community (or character group) without sentimentality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: praised for setting himself the task of portraying the spiritual values of a small Ohio community 'without sentimentality.' Avoid over-emotionalizing; aim for honest presentation of spiritual/ethical life rather than mawkishness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithful regional characterization (short-story regionalism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterization of local/regional types with subtle humor and poetry linked to faithful realism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Miss Babcock's Nantucket folks — 'subtle humor and poetry linked to a faithful realism.' Being a 'leader in short-story regionalism' implies accurate local detail and voice that convey place and people authentically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reticence and restraint (deliberate understatement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of reticence or restraint: not over-stressing points; deliberate understatement to enhance artistic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated praise for 'no point is over-stressed,' 'greater reticence... all to the good,' and 'deliberate understatement.' Anti-pattern: overselling or excessive emphasis that weakens subtlety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegorical clarity and quiet message
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to construct an allegory that quietly sets forth an imaginative attitude or message without sermonizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'The Bell-Tower of P'An-Ku' is an allegory 'quietly setting forth the essence of the imaginative attitude toward life.' Guidance: let the allegory unfold as imagery/tapestry rather than blunt moralizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, swift portraiture capturing national or generational spirit
rubrics_metrics.description: Sharp, economical portraiture that embodies a broader spirit (national/youthful/generational).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Buster' gives 'clear swift portraiture' of America 'youthful and eager, living dangerously and happily.' Use concise, vivid strokes to render individuals who symbolize broader social/psychological types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atmosphere and evocative setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Creation of a convincing atmosphere that evokes nostalgia, place, or dreamlike background enabling reader immersion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'The Black Pearl' is 'an admirable study in atmosphere' and 'atmosphere perfectly realized in brief compass' (Extra Men). Guidance: sustain the mood consistently so readers enter the background 'without difficulty.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Style and stylistic finish
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence (or absence) of distinguishing style; stylistic polish that renders the picture nearly flawless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Style is not a common quality... but the picture portrayed ... is well nigh flawless.' Note: lack of style can be offset by other strengths, but accomplished stories often show a 'finished' stylistic hand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid completeness of detail and suggestive characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of vivid, complete details and suggestive (not exhaustive) characterization that lingers with the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'The Gallowsmith' — 'vivid completeness of detail, and characterization which is admirably suggestive.' Guidance: choose decisive, memorable details that imply more than they state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot management: inevitability with surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: Managing situations so the conclusion feels inevitable yet still unexpected (justifiable surprise endings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: praised where 'its conclusion is inevitable, yet unexpected' and 'one of the best examples of a justifiable surprise ending.' Anti-pattern: surprise that feels contrived or psychologically ungrounded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic economy / concision
rubrics_metrics.description: Economy of expression and plot — telling the essential with minimum waste; a 'finished piece of workmanship.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'exceptional artistic economy,' 'brief tale in sharp outline' described as 'a finished piece of workmanship.' Guidance: prune extraneous material and keep focus on the central incident or idea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychological subtlety and accurate observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Subtle psychological insight into character; close observation of complex or abnormal psychological situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'subtlety of the author's psychology,' 'close observation of abnormal psychological situations,' 'study of suppressed ambition.' Guidance: render internal states delicately rather than in schematic fashion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid oversentimentalizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Resist the temptation to over-sentimentalize themes; maintain reticence and control of tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit admonition: 'The temptation to oversentimentalize the theme must have been almost irresistible, but the author has not failed in reticence.' Anti-pattern: letting sentimentality swamp other artistic virtues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successful use of allegory and symbolic forms (avoid hazards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to use allegory, symbolism, or hazardous literary forms successfully without collapsing into mere rhetoric or preachiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Miss Marks 'steered clear of Scylla and Charybdis successfully' in allegorical stories. Symbolism should be 'woven... modestly' (Lucy Pratt). Anti-pattern: heavy-handed allegory that loses reader engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense of place and cultural detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Realistic, vivid realization of foreign or regional life (Persian, East Indian, Southern Seas, New Orleans, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'vivid realization of Persian life,' 'study of place... one of the best stories so far produced in the literary revival throughout the Middle West.' Guidance: use authentic details to ground the story's world.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of style to subject (voice-fit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Style and sentence rhythm should harmonize with the subject/character; stylistic choices must suit the story's temperament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'If the style is somewhat staccato, this is perhaps in harmony with the character of the story.' Guidance: evaluate whether voice enhances rather than distracts from character and action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic action, stressed conflict, and clear resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of quick dramatic action, well-stressed conflict, clean-cut characterization, and an adequate conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'His Escape' praised for 'quick dramatic action, well stressed conflict, clean-cut characterization, and a thoroughly adequate conclusion.' Guidance: ensure conflict is central and resolved satisfactorily relative to story aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation of mythic or legendary resonance
rubrics_metrics.description: Capacity to create new legends or enduring images that become part of a cultural/literary conversation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'Extra Men' as a 'new legend for American literature' and many war stories creating 'new legends.' Guidance: aim for archetypal or emblematic scenes that transcend mere anecdote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative authenticity: 'made' vs 'told' story
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between stories that feel 'made' (constructed artificially) and those that are 'told' (naturally lived and narrated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique notes 'seems to me a made story rather than a told story' as a weakness. Guidance: favor organic-seeming narration that arises from character and situation rather than contrived plotting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual subtlety of conflict and characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of intellectual subtlety in depicting mental conflicts and contrasting characters so that solutions engage the mind (e.g., like a chess problem).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'The zest of this story consists in the intellectual subtlety of mental conflict... the solution of the story is as absorbing as a chess problem.' Guidance: craft conflicts that reward careful attention and thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of supernatural elements when thematically relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective integration of supernatural beliefs or legends when they bear on the theme (not gratuitous), especially in war stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observation: 'increasing preoccupation with supernatural beliefs... especially as they have a bearing on the fortunes of the war.' Guidance: supernatural elements should deepen theme or psychological reality rather than serve as gimmick.
